root_cause.text: The AF_ALG AEAD control-message handling in `af_alg_cmsg_send()` accepted an unbounded associated-data length (`con->aead_assoclen`) as a 32-bit value, allowing later TX buffer size checks to overflow when very large AD lengths were supplied.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (con->aead_assoclen >= 0x80000000u) return -EINVAL;` immediately after reading `aead_assoclen` from the AEAD control message, and the commit message states this is “to prevent arithmetic overflows when checking the TX buffer size.”

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet shows the new AEAD control-message case in `af_alg_cmsg_send()` that directly stores the user-supplied associated-data length as a 32-bit value: `case ALG_SET_AEAD_ASSOCLEN:` followed by `con->aead_assoclen = *(u32 *)CMSG_DATA(cmsg);`. This matches the root cause of accepting an unbounded AEAD associated-data length in `con->aead_assoclen`, which can later cause TX buffer size checks to overflow. The code only checks `if (cmsg->cmsg_len < CMSG_LEN(sizeof(u32))) return -EINVAL;`, which validates the message size but does not bound the value.
